key_insight: SteelAgent’s apparent predictive accuracy and uncertainty reliability deteriorate when evaluation shifts from random splits to unfamiliar steel families or sources.
engineering_relevance: Steel property estimates used for alloy screening or compliance decisions should identify the evaluation population and avoid assuming reliability on unfamiliar alloys.
method: Combine metallurgical descriptors and machine-learning models with an LLM interface for prediction, uncertainty reporting and inverse design.
Audit generalization using random splits, held-out steel families and held-out sources.
Assess physics-derived features and prediction-interval coverage across evaluation settings.
evidence_signal: On SteelBench tensile-strength evaluations, gradient-boosting pooled out-of-fold R² fell from 0.859 under random splitting to 0.113 with steel families held out; nominal 90% interval coverage ranged from 91.0% on random splits to 37.6% on held-out sources.
watch_item: Physics-derived features are not uniformly beneficial: gradient-boosting R² improved by 0.2534 in a 17-family holdout analysis but declined by 0.358 in a separate four-grade laboratory analysis.
paper_title: SteelAgent: LLM-Orchestrated, Physics-Informed Steel Property Prediction with Audited Generalization and Calibrated Uncertainty
